sections.title: Formal and informal messages: meaning and form
body: Goal: Adapt an invitation, request or cancellation to the reader and purpose.
Core vocabulary: ett ärende, bekräfta, vänliga hälsningar. Key phrases: Jag skriver angående min bokning. · Skulle ni kunna bekräfta tiden? · Hej Mira! Ska vi ses efter jobbet?

A clear message identifies the reader, purpose, essential details and next action. Hej works in many contexts; a service message can end with Vänliga hälsningar, while a friend message may use Hälsningar or Vi ses. Politeness comes from complete, considerate wording, not from unnecessarily old-fashioned language.
Say the examples aloud, notice the pattern, and then change one detail rather than memorising a fixed script.

sections.title: Register, evidence and independent use
body: Register model: “Skulle ni kunna bekräfta tiden?” is a formal-neutral way to express “Could you confirm the appointment?”.
For listening and reading, answer from a specific word or phrase. For speaking and writing, make the recipient, purpose and next action clear.
Attempt the task before using the model. Improve one high-impact feature, then perform it again with the transfer condition.

assignment.title: Four-skill task and transfer
assignment.instructions:
LISTEN: First listen without a transcript. Answer: Who is the intended recipient? Replay once and identify the exact words that prove the answer.

READ: Read for purpose and evidence. Answer: What two things does Dani ask? Mark the shortest phrase that supports your choice.

SPEAK: Give the same cancellation twice: first as a voice message to a close friend, then as a polite call to a course administrator. Make a first attempt, check clarity and repeat once.

WRITE: Write two versions of a request to change a meeting: a brief friend message and a formal-neutral service email. Check reader, purpose, required details and next action.

TRANSFER: The recipient changes from a friend to a manager; keep the facts but adjust opening, request and closing.

BETWEEN LESSON · Optional, 5 minutes: retrieve the three key phrases without looking, then use one in a new sentence.
